payload.title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 5 — English | Tenses
payload.description: Subject-wise test on Tenses (English) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 5. 10Q.
payload.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Identify the tense of the verb in the sentence: My grandmother tells us stories every evening.

options.explanation: The sentence does not describe a past action.
The sentence does not describe a future action.
The sentence does not describe an action in progress.
The sentence describes a habitual action.

questions.explanation: The verb 'tells' is in its base form with 's' for a singular subject, and the phrase 'every evening' indicates a habitual action, which is characteristic of the Present Simple Tense.
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb: The birds ______ sweetly in the morning. (sing)

options.explanation: The sentence does not describe an action in progress.
The base form of the verb is used for a plural subject in the Present Simple Tense.
The sentence does not describe a past action.
The sentence does not describe a future action.

questions.explanation: The birds is a plural subject, and the sentence describes a general or habitual action, requiring the Present Simple Tense. For a plural subject, the base form of the verb is used.
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: Look! The children ______ their new toys now.

options.explanation: The sentence does not describe a habitual action.
The sentence does not describe a past action.
The sentence describes an action in progress.
The sentence does not describe a future action.

questions.explanation: The word 'Look!' and the adverb 'now' indicate an action happening at the moment of speaking, which requires the Present Continuous Tense (are + verb-ing).
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct past tense form of the verb: Last night, my father ______ a delicious dinner. (cook)

options.explanation: The sentence does not describe an action in progress.
The sentence does not describe a habitual action.
The sentence describes a past action.
The sentence does not describe a future action.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'Last night' clearly indicates that the action happened in the past. The simple past tense of 'cook' is 'cooked.'
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Convert the sentence into the Future Tense: Rohan eats an apple.

options.explanation: The sentence describes a past action.
The sentence describes an action in progress.
The sentence describes a habitual action.
The sentence describes a future action.

questions.explanation: To convert a sentence to the Future Tense, we use 'will' or 'shall' followed by the base form of the verb. The base form of 'eats' is 'eat.'
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the Past Tense?

options.text: We go to the zoo tomorrow.
options.explanation: The sentence describes a future action.

options.text: We are going to the zoo now.
options.explanation: The sentence describes an action in progress.

options.text: We will go to the zoo next week.
options.explanation: The sentence describes a future action.

options.text: We went to the zoo yesterday.
options.explanation: The sentence describes a past action.

questions.explanation: The word 'yesterday' indicates an action that happened in the past. 'Went' is the simple past tense of 'go,' correctly matching the time adverb.
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Choose the sentence where the verb tense is used correctly.

options.text: She read a book every day.
options.explanation: The sentence should use the Present Simple Tense for a habitual action.

options.text: He will visited his aunt last month.
options.explanation: The sentence incorrectly uses 'will visited' instead of 'visited' for a past action.

options.text: They are watching television at this moment.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the Present Continuous Tense for an action in progress.

options.text: The cat sleep on the mat now.
options.explanation: The sentence should use the Present Continuous Tense 'is sleeping' or the Present Simple Tense 'sleeps' for a habitual action.

questions.explanation: The sentence 'They are watching television at this moment.' correctly matches the time adverb 'at this moment' with the Present Continuous Tense.
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct tense: Tomorrow, my family ______ to the beach for a picnic.

options.explanation: The sentence does not describe a habitual action.
The sentence does not describe a past action.
The sentence does not describe an action in progress at the moment of speaking.
The sentence describes a future action.

questions.explanation: The word 'Tomorrow' indicates a future action, which requires the Future Simple Tense, formed with 'will' + base verb 'go.'
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence with an incorrect use of tense.

options.text: The sun rises in the east.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the Present Simple Tense for a habitual action.

options.text: My brother is studying for his exam right now.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the Present Continuous Tense for an action in progress.

options.text: The students plays in the ground every afternoon.
options.explanation: The sentence incorrectly uses the singular verb 'plays' with the plural subject 'students.'

options.text: We visited our grandparents last summer.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the Past Simple Tense for a past action.

questions.explanation: The sentence 'The students plays in the ground every afternoon.' incorrectly uses the singular verb 'plays' with the plural subject 'students.'
questions.subject: maha5-english

questions.question: Rearrange the words to form a grammatically correct sentence in the Present Continuous Tense: (is / now / my / drawing / sister / a / picture)

options.text: My sister a picture is drawing now.
options.explanation: The sentence has an incorrect word order.

options.text: Drawing a picture my sister is now.
options.explanation: The sentence has an incorrect word order.

options.text: My sister is drawing a picture now.
options.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the Present Continuous Tense.

options.text: Is my sister drawing a picture now.
options.explanation: The sentence is a question, not a statement.

questions.explanation: The correct sentence structure is Subject + helping verb (is/am/are) + verb-ing + object + time adverb.
questions.subject: maha5-english
